text:
Alex: CI alert just fired for nightly perf — small-batch p95 jumped from ~250ms -> ~420ms on the 8k-seq microbench. Dashboard: https://perf.redwood/example/d/abc123/nightly?panelId=7
Alex: quick paste of the failing metric: 
```
nightly/small-batch/p95 2026-03-18T03:00:00Z 420ms (baseline 250ms)
```
Alex: CI link: https://ci.redwood/example/1234 — job: nightly-smallbatch-8k, unit: kernel-kv-cache
ci-bot: Alert created: nightly-perf/regression (severity: high). Linked issue #INF-487
Priya: ugh. Any obvious config drift? kernel or docker base image changed? 
Marco: I scanned the job history — one commit rolled in a scheduler tweak last night (hash: d9a3f1c). Might be related to yield/backoff change.
Jen: Can someone run a repro on a dev GPU with the same flags? If we can reproduce locally we can capture perf map/prof. Repro command we use: `./tools/bench/run_small.sh --model gpt-small --seq 8192 --batch 4 --iters 100`
Alex: I'm starting a quick reproduce on rdev-gpu-07 with the nightly image. Command: `CI_IMAGE=nightly-2026-03-17 ./tools/bench/run_small.sh --seq 8192 --batch 4`
Marco: If repro is flaky, try with `--prefill 128` to exercise KV hot path. Also add `--log-kv-stats` to get eviction counts.
Priya: Noted. Also checking commit d9a3f1c — it touches scheduler yield timeout default (50ms -> 100ms). Could increase tail for small batches.
Jen: If Alex reproduces, please attach `perf record -ag` for one noisy run and I'll pull flamegraphs. Also add `TOPDOWN=1` env to enable cpu-topdown counters.
Alex: Repro started, first run p95=410ms — so reproducing. Attaching minimal log snippet below:
```
[run 3] p95=412ms p50=90ms kv-evictions=0 tail-queue=8
[run 4] p95=418ms p50=88ms kv-evictions=1 tail-queue=12
```
Alex: Adding perf record now, will upload to /tmp/artifacts/1767894321-perf.tar.gz when done.
ci-bot: Job artifacts uploaded: https://ci.redwood/example/1234/artifacts/1767894321-perf.tar.gz
Marco: I can start a quick bisection off d9a3f1c if we confirm the repro is deterministic enough. Suggest bisect window: last good was ~1767120000 -> range includes scheduler change.
Priya: Also throw in a control run with the old scheduler timeout env `SCHED_YIELD_MS=50` and compare. If that flips p95 back down we have smoking gun.
Jen: Agreed. Alex, can you run two back-to-back: one with `SCHED_YIELD_MS=50` and one with `SCHED_YIELD_MS=100` and paste p95s? No need for perf for both, just metric numbers.
Alex: Running both now. ETA ~5m. Will post numbers.
Alex: Results: `SCHED_YIELD_MS=50` -> p95=256ms; `SCHED_YIELD_MS=100` -> p95=419ms.
Jen: Great repro and clear signal. I'll take the perf tar.gz and look for spin/wait hotspots.
Marco: I'll kick off a narrow bisect later today but given this, we should temp revert the scheduler change on nightly images until we have a fix. Ops: @oncall — can we rollback nightly-image tag?
Priya: Filing quick issue and rollback request: https://issues.redwood/INF-488 (rollback request + test plan).
Alex: Thanks all — looping in eng-sre for rollback. If anyone wants the raw reproducer, it's in the CI job workspace.
Jen: I'll post flamegraphs in this thread when processed. Expect ~30m. :hourglass:
